info.name: Ericsson NCM API
info.description:
# Ericsson Enterprise Wireless NetCloud Manager (NCM) API

Requests for the NCM APIv2 and APIv3, plus a CSV-driven workflow for bulk router configuration changes.

## Setup

### 1. Get API credentials

- **APIv2** (most folders): four keys. See [Obtaining API Keys](https://docs.cradlepoint.com/r/NCM-APIv2-Overview/Obtaining-API-Keys).
- **APIv3** (folders that call `{{v3BaseUrl}}`, including everything marked BETA): a bearer token. See the [NCM API documentation](https://developer.cradlepoint.com/).

### 2. Create an environment

Click the environment dropdown (top right), create an environment such as `NetCloud Manager`, and add:

| Variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `X-ECM-API-ID` | Your ECM API ID |
| `X-ECM-API-KEY` | Your ECM API key |
| `X-CP-API-ID` | Your CP API ID |
| `X-CP-API-KEY` | Your CP API key |
| `NCM_API_TOKEN` | Your APIv3 token |

Enter the raw values without `{{ }}`. Save, then select the environment. Keep credentials in the environment rather than the collection's Variables tab, so they aren't shared if you export or share the collection. The older variable name `TOKEN` still works as an alias for `NCM_API_TOKEN`.

### 3. Test it

Open **Accounts > List Accounts** and click **Send**. A `200 OK` with your account in the body means you're set.

If a request stops with **"Request not sent"**, the console message names the variable that's missing. A `401` usually means a key is wrong or the wrong environment is selected.

## Variables

Requests that need an ID use variables such as `{{router_id}}`, `{{group_id}}` or `{{id}}`. Set them in the collection **Variables** tab, in your environment, or as CSV columns. The pre-request script blocks any request whose variables are empty, so you never send a literal `{{router_id}}` to the API.

`start_time` and `end_time` default to the last 24 hours for endpoints that require a time window.

## API notes

- APIv2 URLs end with `/`. APIv3 URLs do not; a trailing slash can be a 404.
- APIv2 `limit` max is 500. APIv3 `page[size]` max is 50 on most endpoints.
- Several APIv2 sample and log endpoints need a `router` or `net_device` filter. Without it they return `409`.
- A router's `configuration_manager_id` is not its router ID. Look it up with **Configuration Managers > Get Configuration Managers** `?router=<router id>`.
- PATCH on a configuration manager merges changes. PUT replaces the whole configuration.

## Bulk operations with CSV

The Collection Runner can run a request once per CSV row. Column headers must match variable names. A column named `id` is also mapped to `router_id`.

```csv
router_id
1234567
2345678
```

1. Click **Run** on the folder that holds the request.
2. Select only the request you want.
3. Under **Test data file**, choose your CSV.
4. Click **Run Ericsson NCM API**.

## Automation workflows

**Automation Workflows > Bulk Router Configuration Change** applies a configuration change to many routers from a CSV. Its folder description has the setup steps.

item.name: Bulk Router Configuration Change
item.description:
# Bulk Router Configuration Change

Applies the same configuration change to many routers, one CSV row per router.

## How it works

1. **Get Configuration Managers** reads the router identifier from the CSV row and looks up that router's `configuration_manager` ID.
2. **Update Configuration Managers** sends a PATCH with your configuration JSON. Values in the JSON can come from CSV columns.

If a row has no identifier, or no configuration manager matches, the PATCH for that row is skipped and the run moves to the next row.

## Router identifiers

Each CSV row needs one of these columns (checked in this order):

- `id` (router ID)
- `mac`
- `serial_number`

## Setup

1. Build the configuration JSON: make the change in the NCM configuration editor, click **View Pending Changes**, and copy the JSON.
2. Open **Update Configuration Managers** and paste the JSON into the Body tab.
3. Replace values with `{{column_name}}` placeholders that match your CSV columns. Quote string values. For a CSV with an `asset_id` column:

```json
[
  {
    "system": {
      "asset_id": "{{asset_id}}"
    }
  },
  []
]
```

The pre-request script substitutes the CSV values and wraps the body in `{"configuration": ...}` for you.

## Example CSV

```csv
id,asset_id
1234567,STORE-001
2345678,STORE-002
```

## Run it

1. Click **Run** on this folder.
2. Under **Test data file**, click **Select File** and choose your CSV.
3. Click **Run Ericsson NCM API**.

This pushes configuration to live routers. Test with a one-row CSV first.
